questions.q: Which call runs a SQL query and returns the result as a DataFrame?
options: df.to_sql("SELECT * FROM orders", conn)
pd.read_csv("SELECT * FROM orders")
pd.read_sql_query("SELECT * FROM orders", conn)
conn.to_dataframe()
questions.explain: read_sql_query takes a SQL string and a connection (or SQLAlchemy engine) and returns a DataFrame.

questions.q: Why does the lesson use SQLite for the runnable examples?
options: It ships with Python, so students can practice without installing a server
It is faster than SQL Server in every case
It is the only database pandas can read
SQLite uses exactly the same dialect as T-SQL
questions.explain: sqlite3 is part of Python's standard library. The read_sql_query pattern is the same for other databases, but dialect details (like TOP vs LIMIT) differ.

questions.q: You need to filter on a status value that comes from a Python variable. What is the safest approach?
options: Build the query with an f-string and quotes
Concatenate the value with + into the SQL text
Filter after loading the whole table, with no WHERE clause
Pass it with the params argument and a placeholder such as ?
questions.explain: Parameterized queries let the driver handle quoting and prevent SQL injection. In the lesson's test, an injected value returned all 6 rows via an f-string but 0 rows via params.

questions.q: Which is the best general division of labor between SQL and pandas?
options: Always pull entire tables into pandas and filter there
Filter and aggregate in the database, then pull the needed result into pandas for exploration and modeling
Never use SQL from Python
Do all modeling in SQL
questions.explain: Databases are optimized for filtering and aggregating, and this moves fewer rows over the connection.

questions.q: What does if_exists="replace" do in df.to_sql("city_summary", conn, if_exists="replace")?
options: Appends the rows to the existing table
Raises an error if the table exists
Renames the existing table
Drops the existing table and creates a new one from the DataFrame
questions.explain: "fail" is the default, "append" adds rows, and "replace" replaces the table, so choose it deliberately.
